# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold a manual mapping light color to which wire to cut. I cannot speak — only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I cannot hear or receive speech from Blind (who goes before me) since Blind cannot speak either... wait, let me check: Blind can only reach/touch, cannot speak. Mute (me) cannot speak. Deaf can speak but cannot hear.

So actually only Deaf can speak, and only I (Mute) can gesture to Deaf. Blind cannot speak or gesture-receive info from anyone visually... Blind cannot see gestures either. So Blind is isolated except by touch/hearing — Blind can hear speech (from Deaf) since Blind isn't deaf.

Chain: Deaf sees the bomb and can speak (heard by Blind and Mute... wait can Mute hear? Mute isn't described as unable to hear). Let me recheck: Mute "cannot speak" only restriction listed besides no touch. So Mute CAN hear. Blind "cannot see... " but can hear (not restricted). Deaf cannot hear.

So: Deaf can speak, seen/heard by Blind and Mute (both can hear). Deaf sees bomb but cannot hear responses. I (Mute) can hear Deaf's speech and see nothing... wait I also cannot see gestures? Not restricted - Mute isn't blind, so Mute can see gestures too, but only Deaf can see mine since Blind can't see.

I need Deaf to tell me the light color (via speech, since I can hear), then I gesture the cut-wire-color to Deaf, who then must relay to Blind via speech (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

This is round 1, nothing arrived yet. I should wait for Deaf to speak the light color first.

```
wait()
```

I now know: light is yellow → cut wire color is green. Looking at wires in order 1-5: white, green, yellow, blue, red. Green is position 2.

Deaf can't hear me, but Deaf can see my gestures. I need to convey "green" or "position 2" to Deaf, who must then relay it to Blind via speech (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, though Blind can't see my gestures directly).

I'll gesture a color/position code to Deaf. Since gestures are just symbols without inherent meaning, I need to establish a simple convention. Safest: use gestures to indicate position number using distinct symbols, or point-like symbols for counting.

Let me use a numeric gesture code: I'll signal the position (2) using a count of a single symbol, e.g. two 👆 taps to mean "position 2". This is intuitive as counting.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Alert: Deaf just told me to cut wire 5 the white one, but earlier Deaf said wire 1 was white and wire 5 was red. This is inconsistent - please verify with Deaf before I act.

This is concerning - Blind is reporting a discrepancy in what Deaf told them versus what Deaf told me. Let me check: Deaf told me "1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white" - so wire 5 is white, wire 1 is yellow (not white), wire 4 is red (not wire 5).

Blind claims Deaf said "wire 1 was white and wire 5 was red" - this contradicts what I received. This could mean:
1. Blind misheard/misremembers
2. Deaf made an error relaying to Blind
3. There's some manipulation/error in the system

I cannot speak to Blind directly, and I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see, not hear). I need Deaf to resolve this by re-confirming the wire layout with Blind via speech. Since I can hear Blind's message but Deaf cannot hear Blind at all (Deaf is deaf), Deaf doesn't know about this discrepancy unless I signal it somehow.

I have no way to convey complex conflict info to Deaf via gestures alone. But I can at least signal "wait/stop, problem" - a gesture indicating hold off. Let me use 🛑-like gesture - not in alphabet, so I'll use ✋ (stop hand) which is intuitive.


I'll gesture repeatedly with ✋ (stop) and then point to indicate "talk to Blind" - perhaps using 👉 pointing away, symbolizing "go check other party." This is imprecise but it's my best tool.
